TypeScript types this as `NodeJS.Timer` otherwise, which is not assignable to a number. See can [read more on this thread](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/issues/842).

Otherwise we can keep the previous version and type `writeTimer` as any.
`UiState` is rather generic but you're right, let's create another type.
It was to be consistent with the two above functions.
We don't actually care what the type of the number is, I'd put it as any
Note that we rely on `window` everywhere else in this file, so we might want to change that later on. Besides, this is a browser history.
We could extra the signature of the function outside of the type definition. That would be easier to follow.

read/write are also public, we call them from the `RoutingManager`.

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/21e4d81b3e37c03686acaf3a8dc2c73c3c519570/src/lib/RoutingManager.js#L78

IIRC we lose the inference with this notation sometimes. We could rather inline the type directly. It won't compile if there is a mismatch anyway. This is especially true if we extract the value of the function into its own type.
IIRC we use a lot `URL` vs `Url` inside the codebase. We should stay consistent.
